build: PAL cassette, Firebird 1989, analysed in play on level one

comments.text: The game's first instruction, where the tape loader hands over: interrupts off, stack reset, CIA 1 port directions set for the joystick and keyboard, then the NMI, RESET and IRQ vectors at $FFFA-$FFFF pointed at $3A0C (an RTI), $39ED and $3A0D, and $0314 at $3A0D too. CIA 2 selects video bank 3 ($C000-$FFFF), and $01 is written $35, which leaves only I/O over the RAM. It goes on to clear the game flags $42-$44, $53 and $37, run the Hall of Fame prank at $226A and set six lives at $08C0.

The loop the game comes back to after a game: it calls the attract screens ($26DA waits for the fire button on control port 2), clears the top line of the screen at $C000, silences all three SID voices and sets the volume to 15, then plays from $0924; a game that ends returns here with the JMP at $091A.

Sets up a level: clears both screens at $C000 and $C400 and their colour, calls $17B7 and $3DE9, switches $D018 to $0E and $D016 to $18, and gives Rick six bullets ($2D32) and six sticks of dynamite ($2D33) at $09F6. Also reached by the cheat at $0A92, and $09A9 within it after a life is lost.
The game loop: waits until the frame counter $07 is even, so the game moves every second frame (25 times a second on PAL), then calls the routines for one step of play.

Read only when $53 is set (by the name BBOOIINNGG in the Hall of Fame, $2155): one key refills bullets, dynamite and lives to six, another jumps to the level set-up at $0924. Which keys these are depends on the keyboard row selected in $DC00 at the time, not established.

Restores the room's start state from the table at $11A0, then takes one life from $2D34. At zero it writes $C01D and returns; otherwise it sets bit 7 of the first five-byte record holding $16 in the table that $3DCF points at, and restarts from $09A9, with six bullets and six sticks of dynamite.

One step of Hall of Fame name entry: the letter chosen with the joystick is written to the name on screen at $C306. Code $3C rubs out the last letter, $3D ends the name, and a tenth letter ends it too. The game then waits for fire to be released. A finished name goes through the rude-word filter ($2103) and the code words ($2146) and is copied into the table at $2318 ($20E4).
Searches the name just entered, on screen at $C306, for any of the eleven four-letter words in the list at $2181; a name that holds one is replaced by SNIGGER ($21AE).
Compares the entered name with FLUFOMATIC ($21B8), which sets $37, and with BBOOIINNGG ($21C2), which sets $53 and so turns on the cheat keys in the main loop.
Eleven four-letter words the Hall of Fame refuses, ending in a zero: FUCK CUNT PISS SHIT CRAP FART WANK BAST BOLL ARSE BROS. ASCII.
The name that replaces a rude one: SNIGGER, padded with @. ASCII.
FLUFOMATIC, a Hall of Fame name that sets the flag $37. ASCII.
BBOOIINNGG, a Hall of Fame name that sets the cheat flag $53. ASCII.

Called once at power-on. Reads the raster line ($D012) as a random number: when its top bit is set, copies NOBBY or JEZEBEL (bit 3 chooses) from $2368 over one of the Hall of Fame names, chosen by the low three bits (none when they are zero). So the table can differ from one boot to the next.
The eight Hall of Fame names, stored column by column: byte 8 * i + n is letter i of name n, ten letters a name, @ for a space. ASCII.
NOBBY and JEZEBEL, each padded to ten with @: the two names $226A may put into the Hall of Fame. ASCII.
Waits for fire on control port 2 (bit 4 of $DC00), calls $4055, then waits for fire to be released.
GAME OVER, ASCII.
Bullets left, six at the start of each level and after each life lost.
Sticks of dynamite left, six at the start of each level and after each life lost.
Lives left, set to six at $08C0; drawn as hats in the panel.
The RESET vector's target: a loop that flashes the border for ever.
An RTI, so RESTORE does nothing.

The raster interrupt. It works down a list of raster lines through the pointer at $02: each entry picks a handler (its address from the tables at $3BE8 and $3BF9, written into the JMP at $3A3F) and the line of the next interrupt (from $3BD7).
One of the raster handlers: calls $3559 and $36D9, puts the raster list back to its start and counts the frame in $07 ($39F3), then sets $D018 = $0F.

The five story screens, each a 30-character heading padded with @ and lines of text with ~ between paragraphs: South America 1945, Egypt, Europe later that week, Europe even later, and London, much, much later (the ending). ASCII.
